analysis.title: D.R. Horton Inc. (DHI): F4Q26 Recap: Focused Operating Strategy and Impressive Cash Generation Supports Long-Term, Profitable Growth
key_insights: GS maintains Buy on DHI with a 12-month price target of $172, cut from $182, based on 2.0x (unchanged) NTM tangible book value. Price was $146.53, implying 17.4% upside.
GS cuts its F2027 adj. EPS estimate to $8.70 from $11.00 and F2028 to $11.40 from $13.25, in line with the guide and given limited visibility to the selling season. It introduces F2029 EPS at $14.30.

Management described a deceleration in absorptions as consumers turned more cautious into the fall, and this held into October. Traffic is not down as much, which GS reads as intact underlying interest in homeownership.
Buyer profiles are holding, with FICO scores averaging 720 and a cumulative LTV of 90%.

GS argues DHI is positioned for relative outperformance on three points: lower-cost capital than smaller private peers for land acquisition and development, purchasing power and labor retention at scale, and upside to SG&A leverage as conditions normalize.

Full-year CFO guide is $3.5bn, supporting an equal amount of shareholder returns. That reduces the share count 8% YoY and adds about 8% to GS's F2027 EPS estimate. GS also sees potential for smaller bolt-on M&A.

The F1Q guide reflects a slower start to the year. GS sees a path to upward revisions if the mid-term elections pass, the Middle East situation is resolved, and rates, inflation and consumer confidence improve into the spring, helped by easy comps.

DHI offers rate buydowns 1.5pts below the market and smaller footprints. Attached closings are 16% of the mix vs 10% a year ago. Resale competition has intensified, partly offset by share gains. GS also sees some consumers moving down in price.

GS models F1Q homebuilding revenue down 13%, with closings down 10% and ASP down 3% YoY. For F2027 it models closings down 3% (the midpoint of the guide) and homebuilding revenue down 4%, after a 3% contraction in F2026.
With community count growing 7.7% in F2027, GS estimates the sales pace falls 12.2% YoY to 11.3, a cadence not seen since F2017. A return to the more recent pace would imply meaningful upside.

Input costs accounted for 80bps of gross margin compression in the quarter, with warranty and litigation reserves making up the rest. Sticks-and-bricks costs rose 1% sequentially, with lots up 4%. For the full year, materials fell 4% and lot costs rose 6%.
Management cited lumber, near-term freight surcharges from diesel prices, and labor as cost pressures. F1Q gross margin is guided down 100-150bps sequentially and about 270-320bps YoY to 18.0-18.5%.

GS models F2027 home sales gross margin (including amortized interest) at 18.6% and F2027 homebuilding EBIT margin at 9.9%, down 238bps YoY. It says the gross margin estimate could prove conservative if absorptions pick up.
SG&A is running at 9% of annual sales. GS is impressed by the SG&A leverage held while the company funds geographic expansion and higher community count.
GS scenario analysis gives an upside case of $196 (16.8x F2027 EPS) and a downside case of $115 (15.4x F2027 EPS). GS sees favorable risk/reward at the current valuation.
GS estimates revenue of $31,806mn in F2027 (down from the prior $34,059mn), EBITDA of $3,322mn and diluted EPS of $8.70. FY26 revenue was $33,043mn and EPS $10.05.

market_movers.rationale: Buy maintained. Target cut to $172 from $182 on lower F2027-F2029 EPS estimates, set at 2.0x NTM tangible book value. GS cites lower-cost capital, scale and cash generation.

sector_views.rationale: The industry is exposed to affordability pressure, input cost inflation and weaker absorptions. GS sees a lift if macro conditions and rates improve into the spring selling season.

earnings_insights: DHI F4Q26 (fiscal year ended 9/26), reported around 10/28-10/29: FY26 revenue $33,043mn and diluted EPS $10.05 (GS table, FY actual). FY26 revenue growth was -3.5% and EPS growth -13.1%.
F1Q27 guide: gross margin 18.0-18.5%, down 100-150bps sequentially and about 270-320bps YoY. GS models F1Q27 homebuilding revenue down 13%, closings down 10%, ASP down 3%.
F2027 guide: closings down about 3% at the midpoint. GS F2027 estimates: EPS $8.70 (old $11.00), revenue $31,806mn (old $34,059mn), EBITDA $3,322mn. Both are GS estimates, not consensus.
GS quarterly EPS estimates: 12/26E $1.47, 3/27E $1.96, 6/27E $2.84. The 9/26 quarter is $2.67 (GS table).
Full-year F2027 CFO guide is $3.5bn. GS models cash flow from operations of $3,523mn, buybacks of $3,048mn and dividends of $529mn.
GS F2028 EPS estimate $11.40 (old $13.25) and F2029 estimate $14.30 (new).

macro_indicators.interpretation: DHI is using buydowns to support affordability. GS sees a decline in rates as a key swing factor for spring demand.
Buyer credit quality is holding despite the cautious consumer.

risk_factors: Rising mortgage rates and macro uncertainty lower consumer confidence.
Greater-than-expected inflation in land, labor or materials hurts profitability.
Incentives stay higher for longer and pressure margins.
Delays or limits on permitting, inspections and other municipal events.
geopolitical: GS cites an eventual resolution to the situation in the Middle East as a possible driver of lower rates, lower inflation and better consumer confidence into spring.
The mid-term elections are named as a milestone after which conditions could improve.

tension_points.bull_case: A decline in rates, lower inflation and better consumer confidence after the mid-term elections and a Middle East resolution could lift the spring selling season. Traffic is not down as much as absorptions, and comps are easy.
tension_points.bear_case: Absorptions slowed into the fall and October, the F1Q guide is a slower start, resale competition is rising, and input costs and incentives are pressuring margins.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Rising mortgage rates and macro uncertainty that lower consumer confidence, or inflation in land, labor or materials above expectations.

theme_stances.key_argument: Operating leverage and easing inflation and mortgage rates could expand margins in coming quarters.
theme_stances.evidence: we see a path to expansion in the coming quarters

theme_stances.key_argument: Access to lower-cost capital, purchasing power and labor retention leave DHI positioned for industry-relative outperformance.
theme_stances.evidence: uniquely positioned to deliver industry relative outperformance
